description:
Olá a todos! O nosso objetivo neste desafio é conceber um software de monitorização de saúde fiável, preventivo e adaptado às exigências físicas e psicológicas de missões espaciais prolongadas.  

​Pretendemos criar uma ferramenta capaz de transformar dados vitais complexos em decisões rápidas e acionáveis, tanto para a tripulação como para o suporte em terra.

​Valorizamos o trabalho colaborativo, a partilha de ideias e a motivação para entregar um protótipo de excelência.
summary:
ASTRA Health is an autonomous space health decision-support prototype developed by Team ANGARIS to help astronauts monitor their health and respond to potential medical concerns during deep-space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable.

The platform combines simulated vital-sign monitoring, symptom assessment, daily health journals, nine space-health domains, and guided response workflows. It identifies abnormal patterns, distinguishes possible sensor failures from physiological changes, presents scientific evidence, and proposes transparent, rule-based actions for human review.

ASTRA Health also supports extravehicular activity (EVA) decisions, offline operation, and prioritized communication with Earth. Its scientific foundation includes NASA Human Research Program resources and the NASA Open Science Data Repository.

The prototype has documented automated, end-to-end, and scientific verification tests. All physiological data are simulated, and its decision rules and procedures are provisional, not clinically validated.

ASTRA Health demonstrates how evidence-based, human-supervised technology could strengthen astronaut autonomy and health management beyond Earth.
details:
ASTRA Health — Project Details

The Problem

During deep-space missions, astronauts may experience communication delays of 3–22 minutes each way between Mars and Earth. Medical emergencies, physiological changes, equipment failures, and extravehicular activities (EVAs) can require decisions before guidance from Earth becomes available.

ASTRA Health addresses this challenge by demonstrating how astronauts can monitor their health, understand potential risks, and receive structured decision support while operating independently of real-time ground communication.

Our Solution

ASTRA Health is an offline-first, autonomous space health decision-support prototype developed by Team ANGARIS.

The platform follows four core stages:

1. MEASURE — Health Monitoring

Monitors simulated heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and sensor reliability. It identifies abnormal patterns and distinguishes potential sensor failures from physiological deviations.

2. UNDERSTAND — Health Assessment

Uses transparent, deterministic rules to analyze measurements, assess reported symptoms, identify warning signs, and explain findings in accessible language.

The system displays uncertainty, references scientific evidence, and avoids presenting provisional findings as medical diagnoses.

3. ACT — Guided Response

Provides structured demonstration checklists, requests human confirmation, records actions, and proposes escalation when predefined conditions are met.

During EVAs, it supports pre-activity checks, equipment-failure alternatives, incident response, and commander-reviewed decisions.

4. COMMUNICATE — Earth Link

Simulates Earth–Mars communication delays, prioritizes urgent medical reports, stores messages during communication outages, and transmits them when connectivity returns.

Advanced Health Platform — FUTURE Modules

We extended the original prototype with five integrated modules:

  • F01 — Health Journal: Daily astronaut check-ins, symptoms, sleep, hydration, fatigue, scheduled examinations, and longitudinal trends.
  • F02 — Symptom Assessment: Structured symptom evaluation, versioned decision rules, scientific references, uncertainty reporting, and human review.
  • F03 — Space Health Profile: Nine health domains covering neuro-ocular, cardiovascular, renal, radiation, bone/mineral, vascular, immunological, emotional/cognitive, and sleep-related monitoring.
  • F04 — EVA & Autonomous Response: Mission checklists, equipment-aware alternatives, incident management, commander decisions, and priority reporting.
  • F05 — Readiness & Trace: Data-completeness monitoring, system checks, versioned rules, and exportable audit trails.

Unavailable measurements, such as intracranial pressure or bone density, are explicitly identified as missing rather than artificially generated.

Technology and Scientific Resources

ASTRA Health was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and JavaScript, with automated testing through Vitest and Playwright.

The platform uses local browser storage and offline application capabilities to preserve records and support continued operation during simulated communication interruptions.

Its scientific foundation includes NASA Human Research Program publications, Human Research Roadmap resources, and NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset OSD-575, containing cardiovascular biomarker measurements from the Inspiration4 mission.

Scientific research data remain separate from simulated astronaut vital signs. NASA references provide scientific context and do not validate the application's provisional clinical rules.

AI-assisted development tools supported engineering, testing, documentation, and presentation. Medical decision proposals in the demonstrated system are generated by deterministic rules rather than generative AI.

Testing and Validation

The team documented the following successful software verification results:

  • 184/184 automated tests passed, combining original and FUTURE suites.
  • 31/31 end-to-end browser checks passed, including regression tests.
  • 32/32 scientific source-verification checks passed.
  • Zero violations detected in the automated accessibility audit across 29 checks.

The platform also demonstrates offline operation, prioritized message synchronization, human decision logging, and detection of alterations to its audit trail.

These results verify specified software behavior; they do not constitute clinical validation.

Innovation and Impact

ASTRA Health's key innovation is combining continuous health monitoring, longitudinal astronaut records, evidence-based context, structured symptom assessment, autonomous offline workflows, and human-supervised operational decisions in one integrated platform.

Rather than relying on continuous communication with Earth, the system demonstrates how crews could maintain situational awareness and follow transparent decision-support workflows during communication delays or outages.

The concept may inform future research into medical autonomy for lunar and Martian missions, remote expeditions, and other environments with limited access to healthcare professionals.

Safety and Limitations

ASTRA Health is a research and demonstration prototype, not a medical device.

All astronaut physiological data are simulated or entered during demonstrations. Medical thresholds, decision rules, and response procedures are provisional, have not been clinically validated, and are not endorsed by NASA.

Human crew members remain responsible for operational decisions.
